catalog_quote: A. Acento. Consideramos que el acento en esta lengua es un rasgo suprasegmental que caracteriza la palabra (ver definición de la palabra en el capítulo de Morfología). El acento permite distinguir palabras lexemáticas simples de palabras morfológicamente complejas. Fonéticamente el acento kogui es de intensidad aunque conlleva rasgo de altura, notoria sobre todo en palabras acentuadas en la última sílaba, cuando ésta es un morfema gramatical. La mayor parte de las palabras monomorfemáticas del kogui, tiene el acento en la penúltima sílaba y son bisílabas. Hay un pequeño porcentaje de palabras bisílabas agudas y de palabras esdrújulas. new_statements.translation: Phonetically the Kogui accent is one of intensity although it carries a pitch feature, noticeable above all in words accented on the last syllable when this is a grammatical morpheme. Most monomorphemic words of Kogui have the accent on the penultimate syllable and are disyllabic. There is a small percentage of oxytone disyllabic words and of proparoxytone words. There is an opposition between lexemes due to the position of the accent, which can be shown: kala 'straw' / ka'la 'leg'; nugi 'poporo lime' / nu'gi 'plague', 'crazy' [...] c. When the word has suffixed grammatical morphemes that are accented, the lexeme loses its own accent in favour of that morpheme, which attracts the word accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level stress (intensity) accent. Default/majority pattern: penultimate syllable in monomorphemic words (mostly disyllables), but position is lexically contrastive (minority of final- and antepenult-stressed words, minimal pairs). In complex words the accent moves: inherently accented suffixes attract the single word accent; verb-final accent marks the preterite. SIL orthography (Gawthorne & Hensarling 1984 §7) corroborates: the accent mark is written only when stress is NOT penultimate.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In compound words of four or more syllables a secondary accent is perceived on the syllable that bore the accent of the lexeme in its free form (p. 760).
new_statements.exceptions: A 'small percentage' of oxytone disyllables and proparoxytones; lexical minimal pairs (kála/kalá 'straw/leg', núgi/nugí, múnʒi/munʒí 'woman/malanga', múgi/mugí); accented suffixes (e.g. negative-interrogative -kí) override the lexeme's accent; final accent on verbs = preterite.
new_statements.domain_note: The word (defined on p. 766 as the stretch of speech carrying one accent); statement concerns monomorphemic citation forms, with separate rules for compounds and suffixed words. Author treats accent as distinctive; a stricter reading would be 'lexical with penultimate default'.
new_statements.identity_note: Ortíz Ricaurte 2000 describes Kogui as spoken on the northern slope of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (data mainly from mama Juan Conchacala Dingula, San Miguel/Anche-Palomino-Don Diego valleys); same language as Glottolog cogu1240 (Kogi/Cogui/Kággaba, ISO kog); no dialect split is made.
